verdicts.reasoning: These items require the student to identify the specific type of surface (e.g., flat or curved) that belongs to given solid figures like cans, boxes, and balls.
These questions specifically prompt the student to explain reasoning by asking 'Why?' or 'How is... different?', requiring them to select the underlying rationale for geometric properties.
These items explicitly ask the student to contrast two concepts, detailing the difference between rolling versus non-rolling objects or straight versus curved lines.
The concept of straight lines is directly assessed by asking students to distinguish their core property (never bending) and relate them to real-world objects like a ruler's edge.
These samples explicitly target curved lines, challenging the student to understand how they bend smoothly in comparison to straight lines or identifying them in objects like the rim of a plate.
These seeds actively operate on the concept of 'flat' surfaces, testing the student's ability to map this property to relevant 3D shapes like boxes and the ends of a can.
The items successfully require the application of 'curved surfaces' as a concept, prompting the student to identify the rounded features of balls and cans.
The geometric questions are appropriately framed around tangible 3-dimensional objects (balls, boxes, cans), linking abstract surface concepts to solid physical forms.
